clue.text: Go along with unfashionable crowd

parts.note: a go in a game is a turn
something unfashionable is out

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly falls in with an unstylish group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the crowd of people who attend an event.

clue.text: Sailor turned up to travel around island

indicators.note: around means the to-travel pair wraps the sailor

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to travel

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman arrived to tour an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read upwards; 'around' puts the turned sailor inside the to-travel pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Explorer and artist pursued by actress

indicators.note: pursued by means the artist comes first, followed by the actress

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
Vivien Leigh was a film actress

explanation.surface: An explorer and a painter being chased by a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan explorer of the Americas.

clue.text: Toes broken on old pavement — see medical specialist

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: a path is a pavement or footway

explanation.surface: After stubbing your toes on an ancient pavement, consult a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the body by manipulating bones and muscles.

clue.text: Old port in booty recovered

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the next words

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are retrieved in an ancient harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre was an ancient Phoenician seaport, now in Lebanon.

clue.text: In which the present opportunities are felt to be uncertain?

definitions.text: In which the present opportunities are felt to be uncertain?

parts.words: In which the present opportunities are felt to be uncertain
parts.note: reads like a comment on today's shaky prospects, but describes a fairground dip where wrapped gifts are groped for blindly in bran

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about how insecure today's openings feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' means a gift, not 'current', and 'felt' means touched by hand. A BRAN TUB is a British fete game: a tub of bran with prizes buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a lucky-dip tub, prizes hidden in bran are found by touch, so what you get is a matter of chance.

clue.text: Political strategy? Vile mobs ordered to keep quiet!

indicators.note: to keep means to hold the next piece inside
ordered means put into a different order

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A political plan: the nasty rabble are told to be silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' shuffles VILE MOBS to BOLEVISM, and 'to keep' puts SH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshevism was the revolutionary political doctrine of Lenin's party.

clue.text: One of an ancient people with a name from Ireland

parts.note: Ryan is a common Irish name

explanation.surface: A member of an early race carrying an Irish name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aryans were an ancient Indo-Iranian people.

clue.text: Army fellow without name or function

indicators.note: without means outside, so the army fellow wraps the name

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve
a gent is a fellow

explanation.surface: A soldier with no name and no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangent is a trigonometric function.

clue.text: Mount with French soldier buried in cemetery

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: to mount a ship or train is to board it
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A horseman and a French soldier laid to rest in a graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A boneyard is an informal word for a cemetery.

clue.text: British friend, one subsequently imprisoned for helping both sides?

indicators.note: imprisoned means the next pieces are held inside the British friend pair

parts.note: an ally is a friend
the Roman numeral I is one
subsequently means later

explanation.surface: A British friend was later jailed for aiding both parties in a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' means the British friend pair is split open to hold the one-subsequently pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting bilaterally means acting on behalf of, or affecting, two parties at once.

clue.text: Joshua's father, a religious person

definitions.meaning: in the Bible, Joshua is called the son of ...
a woman in a religious order, living in a convent

explanation.surface: A Biblical patriarch is described as a devout individual.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Joshua names his father as Nun, and a nun is also a woman under religious vows.

clue.text: Standard set by good Scottish side on the field

parts.note: guid is the Scots form of good
in cricket the on side is the leg side of the field

explanation.surface: A banner is raised by a fine Scottish team playing on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidon is a small flag or pennant carried by a military unit, a kind of standard.

clue.text: Opportunist — last character you want in jury in court

parts.note: a chancer is someone who seizes any opportunity

indicators.note: the final letter of the word jury is taken

explanation.surface: A complaint about a chancer you want to have serving on a jury in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of the English High Court.

clue.text: Improve efficiency of inert males with training

indicators.note: training shapes and reforms, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Getting lazy men into shape through exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline an organisation is to make it more efficient.

clue.text: A liverish tot treated by hospital nurse

indicators.note: treated as in processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child with a liver complaint is seen by a hospital nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' shuffles A LIVERISH TOT together with H for hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a health visitor is a community nurse who visits families with young children.

clue.text: Feature of cliff in Kent resort

definitions.meaning: a town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, an English county

explanation.surface: The steep drop of a cliff at a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a Kent seaside town, and sheerness is also the vertical steepness of a cliff face.

clue.text: Fellow initially demeaned blossomed

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

parts.note: to demean someone is to lower them

explanation.surface: A man first humiliated later flourished.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowered has blossomed.

clue.text: What could be the nice silent bit of Europe

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Wondering which pleasantly quiet part of the continent this might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray B in the held clue is a scanning mark; the page prints 'bit of Europe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liechtenstein is a tiny principality in central Europe, so a small bit of the continent.

clue.text: Stones thrown by hostile characters

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed into disorder

explanation.surface: Rocks are hurled by enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' just says HOSTILE is used for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoliths are crudely chipped flints thought to be early stone tools.

clue.text: Like the smarter set, I featured in gossip

indicators.note: featured in means placed inside the next piece

parts.note: natter means chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: I appeared in the society chatter about the fashionable crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart, so the smarter set are nattier.

clue.text: Rather small-minded rules initially introduced

indicators.note: introduced means inserted into the next piece

parts.note: petty means small-minded

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Somewhat narrow regulations were brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty can mean rather or fairly, as in pretty good.

clue.text: We'll grab everyone good in the morning for school sport

indicators.note: to grab is to hold, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: the word we, with 'll only turning the surface to the future
all means everyone
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: We will seize everybody fine before noon for a game at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The WALL GAME is a ball game played only at Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton wall game is a sport played at Eton College against a long brick wall.

clue.text: Mollusc to get one staring

definitions.meaning: a large burrowing clam with a gaping shell
someone who gapes or stares open-mouthed

explanation.surface: A shellfish ends up with someone gawping at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gaper is a burrowing clam, and a gaper is also a person who stares.

clue.text: It makes small bits of food larger, so they say

definitions.text: It makes small bits of food

indicators.note: so they say means the word is spoken and heard

parts.note: larger means greater

explanation.surface: Something that enlarges small morsels of food, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'makes small bits of food larger'; the definition stops at 'food'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen grater shreds cheese or vegetables into small pieces.

clue.text: Handed over power, given support

indicators.note: given means the second piece is added on

parts.note: aid is support

explanation.surface: Power was transferred, and support provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid means handed over money.

clue.text: Grass or speed but not Ecstasy

indicators.note: but not means the next piece is left out

parts.note: a rate is a speed
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A list of drugs: cannabis or amphetamine, but no Ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass and speed look like drugs; grass is the definition, meaning inform.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform on them, the same as to grass, a British slang verb.

clue.text: After letter from abroad one may get recent catalogue

definitions.text: After letter from abroad one may get recent catalogue

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
late can mean recent, as in the late news
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: Someone who is after letters from foreign countries may receive the latest catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp collector seeks foreign mail and gets dealers' catalogues of new issues.

clue.text: Girl's father plunged in river

definitions.note: Girl's stands for girl is, the name being the subject

indicators.note: plunged in means put inside the next piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales
a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A young woman's dad dived into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiree is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Get rid of tyrant wanting old city for trophy

indicators.note: wanting means the tyrant word needs a substitution
for means one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: a despot is a tyrant
a pot is a slang word for a trophy or cup
Troy is the ancient city of the Iliad

explanation.surface: Overthrow a tyrant who covets an ancient city as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting old city for trophy': DESPOT puts TROY in place of POT.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to get rid of it entirely.
